purpose: Requirement-derived native case/control plan for the accepted default-home current-login flow. This is data, not runnable tests, a bound Interpreter scenario or an execution report. Each case uses a fresh disposable fixture unless its operations explicitly share state. Expectations precede execution; identifiers beginning with $ are fixture-owned. Assert environment and custody independently so one failure does not hide another.

boundaries.synthetic: Scratch Git/worktree and HOME; injected Git/GitHub, Herdr inventories/agent observations, native-session metadata lookup, environment, filesystem/atomic checkpoint failures, wall/elapsed clocks, sleep, confirmation and terminal attachment. Exercise actual generated shell commands with a harmless Codex stub printing only synthetic HOME, CODEX_HOME and argv. Use existing public functions and factory handles; no check-only production API or hand-edited real run records.
boundaries.unsupported: These cases do not prove provider login/quota, running Codex authentication reload on Continue, real saved-session loading, transport delivery to a real agent, filesystem races beyond tested interleavings or acceptance in another pane. No credential or transcript read, real sign-in/home mutation, model call or live Herdr effect belongs in synthetic controls.

criteria.text: After I change the login in the same default Codex home, I can type Continue in the existing conversation. PDD does not create a fresh conversation just because that login changed.

When PDD starts a default-home Codex chat, its child uses the machine home selected when the run started and no unrelated CODEX_HOME inherited from the Herdr server or pane. Later areas keep that home even when approved from another terminal.

If the original process has ended and a restart is needed, ordinary `pdd workflow open 2575` resumes the exact saved native conversation in the assigned worktree, using that selected home. The issue, run, branch, completed steps, gate, question, decisions, approvals and PR records stay intact.

Opening a healthy live conversation focuses it without another launch. A quota error, missing observation, unknown ownership or unresolved launch does not authorize a duplicate process, a fresh conversation or a blind restart. A live question dialog keeps its existing protection.

PDD recognizes the exact conversation resumed in its owned pane as running. A retained pending request reaches that conversation once on safe explicit retry, with the same request identity; it is never redirected to another area or session and does not rewind workflow progress.

Older runs without a saved machine home remain readable. Before their next required native start or resume, PDD selects and saves the invoking machine home once; status or focus alone does not select one, and a failed checkpoint launches nothing.

Explicit CODEX_HOME plus `--new` remains the separate fresh-conversation fallback, preserving its existing profile selection, attempt recovery, cancellation and identity safeguards. Other agents keep their existing behavior. PDD does not read or change credentials, migrate homes or change global sign-ins.

The CLI documentation explains Continue in the same default home, exact-conversation resume when needed, and the separate fresh-conversation fallback, without claiming that a selected folder proves the active login or authentication reload.
